extracted.intended_audience: graduate students applying for NIA F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research (predoctoral-to-postdoctoral) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH NIA F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research fellowship application (two-phase predoctoral F99 and postdoctoral K00 stages), including SF 424 forms, PHS fellowship supplemental materials, human subjects protection, facilities/resources, and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: F99/K00 two-phase structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research for Predoctoral Students Awards, NIA supports exceptional graduate students in finishing their dissertation research on any topic and continuing to a postdoctoral position conducting research on aging. Each award has two phases: the F99 phase supporting predoctoral training and the K00 phase supporting postdoctoral training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must describe both the predoctoral (F99) training and research plan and the proposed postdoctoral (K00) training and research plan; the K00 stage should be framed as a transition to independent postdoctoral research in aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and credit/copyright notice for sample application material
rubrics_metrics.description: The awardee allows you to use the material (e.g. data, writing, graphics) in their application only for nonprofit educational purposes, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigator, awardee organization, and NIH NIA are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reusing content from the sample, keep it unchanged and include appropriate credits; do not repurpose without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference latest Fellowship Instructions and FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that these applications do not reflect the new Fellowship review criteria, effective January 25, 2025, as well as other updates to application instructions. Be sure to refer to the latest Fellowship Instructions and the current Notice of Funding Opportunity when preparing an F99/K00 application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must verify and follow the current NIH fellowship instructions and the specific FOA; sample content may be out of date.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) required fields and cover information
rubrics_metrics.description: The SF 424 (R&R) Cover Page must include Type of Submission, Date Submitted, Applicant Information (legal name, department, address), Project Director/PI contact information, Project start/end dates, Congressional district, and other administrative identifiers (DUNS, EIN, Grants.gov tracking numbers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all mandatory SF 424 fields accurately. The cover includes applicant organizational info, authorized representative signature, and certifies compliance with assurances and certifications (Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, assurances, and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the authorized representative certifies to the statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances, and that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of their knowledge; aware that false statements may lead to penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authorized institutional official must sign the application and date it; include required certification documents or link to them as specified in agency instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Include SF 424 R&R Cover Page; Table of Contents; Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary/Abstract(Description); Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Other Attachments; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; PHS Fellowship Supplemental with specified subheadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all listed attachments and forms are present and correctly named (Project Summary, Project Narrative, Bibliography, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Other Attachments, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Introduction (for resubmissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If resubmitting, include an Introduction that addresses prior review critiques and revisions made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise rebuttal/response to reviewers and description of changes; follow page limits and instructions for resubmission introductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the applicant’s background, dissertation progress, and short- and long-term career goals for training in aging research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the fellowship will enable completion of dissertation and transition to postdoctoral research; provide evidence of preparedness and fit for the proposed training.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: List clear Specific Aims for the proposed dissertation and for the postdoctoral phase as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concise, testable, and aligned with methods and outcomes; include overarching aim for K00 if required (e.g., develop intervention).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the research plan (background/significance, preliminary data if any, methods, analyses) for the dissertation (F99) and for the proposed K00 work where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe study design, datasets (e.g., NHATS waves 5–9), analytic methods (e.g., multi-level modeling, structural equation modeling), sample characteristics, and how the plan is feasible within the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Respective Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the contributions of the applicant and key mentors/co-sponsors to the proposed research and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles, division of labor, and supervisory/training responsibilities among PD/PI, sponsor, co-sponsors, and collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Selection of Sponsor and Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain rationale for choice of sponsor(s) and institution(s) for both F99 and K00 phases; describe how mentor(s) will support training goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of mentor expertise, institutional commitment, and access to relevant resources, cores, datasets, and training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe planned training in responsible conduct of research for the fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include content, format, frequency, faculty involved, and institutional RCR curriculum; follow NIH RCR requirements for fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Sponsor and Co-Sponsor Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide signed statements from sponsor and co-sponsors describing mentoring plan, time commitment, and support for applicant’s training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor statements should detail mentoring approach, oversight, career development plans, and specifics of support at F99 and K00 stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters from collaborators and consultants that confirm availability, role, and contributions to the project or training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be specific about resources, data access, collaborations, and commitments; avoid generic letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental — Description of Institutional Environment and Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional resources, centers, cores, IT services, and programs that will support the fellow’s training and research (e.g., USC SSW, ADRC, OHSU OADC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List facilities, equipment, access to datasets, training workshops, administrative support, and how the environment is suited for aging research and fellowship success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a succinct summary describing aims, background, significance, methods, datasets, and anticipated outcomes for both F99 and K00 phases (e.g., dissertation will analyze NHATS data; K00 will include systematic review and analysis of I-CONECT and CART datasets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary should concisely state the problem, approach, and potential impact; include dataset names, analytic methods, and overarching goals for career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: State the public health relevance and how the proposed research will contribute to knowledge (e.g., longitudinal empirical evidence on environment, social isolation, and cognitive health; development of an intervention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the research addresses health-related priorities and potential beneficiaries; keep concise and accessible to a lay reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete citations for literature cited in the application (e.g., references on social isolation, ICT use, environmental influences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include up-to-date, relevant literature supporting significance, prior work, and chosen methods; follow citation format required by application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the physical, intellectual, and institutional resources available (e.g., research space, IT services, cores, ADRC REC, collaborative relationships, training opportunities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how institutional resources will support the project and training; include specifics (software available, secure data storage, teleconferencing, cores, data access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available or requested and justify need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no major equipment is needed, include a 'No Major Equipment' statement/file; otherwise document equipment location and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Attachments (e.g., Certification letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach required other documents such as Certification Letter, Cover Letter, authentication documentation, inclusion enrollment reports, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name attachments clearly and include any institutional or sponsor letters required by the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches, roles, and contact information for senior/key personnel (PD/PI, sponsor, co-sponsors, other key staff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure key personnel are listed with correct role categories and that their commitments are consistent with sponsor statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information / Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Human Subjects Involvement, characteristics, design; whether the project is exempt; IRB approval status; vertebrate animals; proprietary information; environmental impact; international activities; human subjects risks and protections; recruitment and consent; confidentiality; data storage; and potential benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive human subjects sections: (a) Human Subjects Involvement, Characteristics, and Design; (b) Study Procedures and Materials; (c) Potential Risks; (d) Adequacy of Protection Against Risks (including Informed Consent and Assent); (e) Potential Benefits; (f) Importance of the Knowledge to be Gained. Include statements on exemptions and supporting IRB numbers if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Exemption and IRB details
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if human subjects are involved and whether the project is exempt under specific exemption numbers; provide IRB approval dates or indicate if pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exempt, list the appropriate exemption numbers; if not exempt, provide IRB review status and approval dates and Human Subject Assurance Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Study Procedures and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures for both secondary data analysis (e.g., NHATS waves 5–9) and primary data collection (e.g., I-CONECT, CART, focus groups), including recruitment, intervention procedures, assessment schedules, recordings, and in-home monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how data will be collected or accessed, frequency and duration of contacts, recording/transcription plans, and any device or sensor use; specify de-identification and data handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Informed consent and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe informed consent procedures for primary data (e.g., focus groups), how consent will be documented, storage of consent forms, protections for potentially vulnerable populations (e.g., MCI participants), and personnel training (IRB training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain recruitment contact, consent presentation and signing, storage and retention of consent forms, steps to protect confidentiality (separate files for contact info), and training of research assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Confidentiality and data security
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures to reduce confidentiality risk (de-identification of secondary datasets, password-protected files, locked cabinets, restricted access), and plans for data destruction or long-term storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how identifying information will be handled, who will have access, where data will be stored, and timelines for destruction of raw materials if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Potential risks and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential risks (e.g., mild discomfort from discussing social isolation), plan to minimize risks, participant rights (right not to answer, withdraw), compensation, and transport arrangements for focus groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain monitoring of adverse events, referral plans if distress occurs, and measures to prevent contamination between intervention and qualitative sampling (e.g., only invite participants who have completed I-CONECT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Benefits and importance of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe direct and indirect benefits to participants and the importance of knowledge to be gained (e.g., informing interventions, policy, aging-in-place strategies, and developing ICT-facilitated programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate how the research will contribute to scientific understanding, public health, or participant well-being; tie anticipated benefits back to aims and dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Synopsis / Study Design elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a protocol synopsis including Study Design (detailed description), Primary Purpose, Interventions (type, name, description), Study Phase, Intervention Model, Masking, Allocation, Outcome Measures (type, name, time frame, brief description), Statistical Design and Power, Subject Participation Duration, FDA-regulated intervention status, and Dissemination Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials or intervention studies, fully describe design choices (randomization, masking), outcome definitions and timing, power calculations, and plans for reporting and dissemination. Indicate if the study is an NIH-defined Phase III clinical trial or an FDA-applicable trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (DSMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board will be appointed and describe the overall data and safety monitoring plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For trials or higher-risk studies, describe DSMB composition, monitoring frequency, stopping rules, and reporting pathways; if no DSMB, justify and describe alternative monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If key biological or chemical resources are used, provide authentication plans; otherwise state that no key biological/chemical resources will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures for authentication and documentation of sources/quality for reagents, cell lines, antibodies, etc., when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Reports and Reporting Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include inclusion/enrollment reporting materials and be prepared to report participant demographics and enrollment over time as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FOA and NIH policies on inclusion of women, minorities, and children, and provide enrollment/monitoring plans and reporting formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how study results will be disseminated (e.g., publications, conferences, community engagement) and how findings will inform intervention design or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for manuscripts, presentations, stakeholder engagement, and possible data sharing consistent with participant confidentiality and NIH/data-use policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/resubmission indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Document administrative metadata (Funding Opportunity Number, Received Date, Council date, Competition ID, Accession Number, IPF, Organization, Department, IRG/SRG, AIDS designation, Clinical Trial designation, Human Subjects/Animals flags, HS Code, HESC, HFT, New Investigator status, Senior/Key Personnel listings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all administrative tags are accurately recorded on submission for routing, review assignment, and compliance checks.
